title: Blob Storage: containers, blobs and the three blob types

videos.script: Lesson 1 met the storage account and made a container in it, and left a question open. What is a blob, exactly? {{blob}} It is a name and some bytes, in a container. The slashes in the name look like folders. They are not. {{folders}} You will list three nightly exports and watch a folder appear that nobody created. {{listing}} Then the three kinds of blob. A block blob is built from blocks, and it only exists once they are committed. {{blocks}} An append blob only grows at the end, which is what a log wants. A page blob is a disk, in pages of 512 bytes. {{types}} Every blob also carries a description: properties the service fills in, and metadata you write yourself. {{metadata}} And one of those properties, the ETag, stops two copies of a job from overwriting each other without knowing. {{etag}} By the end you can say which type a file should be, and how to write it safely when two programs share it. {{end}}
